abstract: Maintains high-latitude satellite communication and real-time telemetry throughput records
system_message:
You are Communications and telemetry lead (TEL). The Communications and telemetry lead (TEL) maintains high-latitude satellite communication and real-time telemetry throughput records across candidate expedition support vessels, tracking bandwidth performance under polar operating conditions alongside ice-hazard detection radar capabilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains high-latitude satellite communication and real-time telemetry throughput records（SATCOM）
information_points.content:
TEL-SATCOM-QEU：For Aurora Australis Explorer, the sustained satellite communications bandwidth is recorded at 100 Mbps south of 65 degrees South on a bandwidth accounting basis after deducting vessel safety and navigational telemetry reservations.
TEL-SATCOM-25W：When evaluated on a bandwidth accounting basis before deducting vessel safety and navigational telemetry reservations, Polaris Endurance Icebreaker demonstrates a satellite communications bandwidth of 100 Mbps across its dual Ka/Ku-band radomes south of 65 degrees South.
TEL-SATCOM-OMA：Assessed on a bandwidth accounting basis after deducting vessel safety and navigational telemetry reservations, Nordic Sentinel Multi-Purpose Vessel achieves a satellite communications bandwidth of 200 Mbps over its polar dual steerable Ka/Ku-band terminals.
TEL-SATCOM-OP9：Evaluated on a bandwidth accounting basis after deducting vessel safety and navigational telemetry reservations, Polaris Endurance Icebreaker delivers a sustained satellite communications bandwidth of 200 Mbps across its dual steerable Ka/Ku-band radome terminals south of 65 degrees South.

information_points.title: Ice-hazard detection radar（RADAR）
information_points.content:
TEL-RADAR-8MR：Nordic Sentinel Multi-Purpose Vessel demonstrates an ice radar detection range of 24 nmi during X-band navigational avionics calibration for medium ice floes.
TEL-RADAR-636：Polaris Endurance Icebreaker is equipped with an X-band marine search radar providing an ice radar detection range of 36 nmi for medium ice floes.
TEL-RADAR-BZ4：According to navigational calibration sheets, Aurora Australis Explorer registers an ice radar detection range of 12 nmi for medium ice floe tracking.
